newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas still mostly up late, ranges hold.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas still mostly up late, ranges hold.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, helped by a relatively steady physical market, mostly held slim gains late Wednesday in moderate trade, but prices were still bound in recent technical ranges.
At 1425 EDT, June edged up 0.4 cent to $2.195 per million British thermal units after dipping early to $2.16. July was one-half cent higher at $2.235. Most others also were up.

"We're definitely stuck in a technical range. The fundamentals are not real strong either way and there's a lack of conviction," said one Texas trader, adding some Midwest cold and western heat helped underpin the cash this month.

"I've been leaning bearish for a while, but there's been hot weather in the West and some overnight heating load in the Midwest and just enough injection demand to hold the cash up," the Texas trader said, adding the likely onset soon of the summer air conditioning season may have tilted the scales in favor of the bulls now.

But others noted the relatively large open interest which could leave the market vulnerable to a sharp selloff, particularly when funds liquidate. And forecasts for mostly seasonal to below-seasonl weather for much of the nation also offered little hope for better cooling demand near-term.

Technical traders agreed recent ranges were intact, with June support and resistance still at $2.15 and $2.30, respectively. Major buying should emerge at the $2.05 double bottom, with good selling likely at the $2.43 contract high.
A Reuter poll of industry players showed most expected a weekly stock build in the 55-65 bcf range when AGA data are released later today. Last year, stocks gained 59 bcf.

In the cash Wednesday, Gulf Coast swing prices were steady to down slightly in the high-teens. Midcon pipes were little changed at about $2.00. New York city gate gas also held relatively steady in the mid-$2.40s.
Maintenance on Transco's Texas line will continue to cut about 400 mmcfd out of a total capacity of about 600 mmcfd through Thursday.

Planned work on Mobil's Mary Ann gas processing plant in Coden, Ala., has cut the plant's total processing capacity of 380-390 mmcfd. About 120 mmcfd should be back within the next seven days, with the balance due back in three weeks.
NYMEX said 26,438 contracts traded at 1330 EDT. Hub open interest on May 20 rose 3,015 contracts to 208,220.
On the KCBT, June was unchanged at $2.045, while deferreds remained narrowly mixed. The East/West spread widened by one-half cent to 15.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
